headline: Bamboo's compiler refuses the merge-at-runtime `css()` call that costs `panda` 13.4 ms/1k, so the same Panda-shaped API lands at the static-class floor once variant selection is forced into `cx()` over precompiled literals.

microbench.why: `next-yak-9.7` compiles the variant into `$prop` class toggles that fold to a string concat, so it renders at 0.601 ms/1k. The case's real lesson is `panda` against `bamboo`: both expose the same `css()` API, but `panda` merges the conditional objects at render (13.4 ms/1k, 15.1 ms of component self-time) while `bamboo`'s compiler rejects a conditional inside one `css()` call, forcing five static calls joined by `cx()` that compile to class-string literals, and it renders at 0.647. `panda`'s own precompiled `cva` recipe confirms the mechanism at 0.941 ms/1k, and the hashers sit between at `styled-components` 1.85 and `emotion` 2.81.

autocannon.why: The same split holds under load: `next-yak-9.7` serves 1535 req/s and `bamboo` 976 against `panda`'s 72, which re-merges the variant objects on every request. `panda`'s `cva` recipe recovers to 752 req/s from identical CSS. `emotion` (339) and `styled-components` (516) pay their hash per request rather than per variant.

attribution.why: Where the class string is decided at build time the render is react-dom and little else: `vanilla`, `next-yak-css-9.7` and `stylex-layers` land at 0.691-0.695 ms with a library slice at or near zero. `panda` puts 15.1 of its 15.8 ms into component self-time, 428 ms of a 450 ms JS window inside its own package, resolving merged objects to atomic classes per element. `bamboo` runs the identical API at 0.729 ms with a 0.013 ms library slice, the whole difference being that its `cx()` joins literals the compiler already produced.

top3.label: StyleX without CSS layers (:not() specificity hack)

hydrate.why: The variant button hydrates as pure JS wherever the sheet is a file, 44.8-52.1 ms for the folded, StyleX and `bamboo` builds, with 0 ms of style and layout inside the span. `panda`'s `css()` re-resolves the variants on the client and lands at 105 ms, while `goober` (97.5 ms) and `styled-components` (102 ms) inject and pay 0.21 ms of recalc plus a 1.2-1.6 ms layout inside the span. Spreads inside the fast cluster reach 45%, so its internal order carries no signal.

inp.why: Toggling the variant re-renders one button, and every lane that decided its class at build time does the toggle as a string swap: 6.9-8.1 ms across them, one measurement. `panda` re-runs the merge on the interaction and needs 48.0 ms, the only lane where changing a variant costs real work. `goober` shows a 2.13 ms JS slice against the cluster's 0.4-0.7 and is still invisible in the frame.

top3.label: StyleX without CSS layers (:not() specificity hack)

mount.why: Cold mount is one sheet parse plus first paint, 75.5-79.1 ms for the build-time lanes. `panda` does its render-time merge before that paint and reaches 133 ms, `emotion` 106 and `styled-components` 93.2. `bamboo` mounts at 80.5 ms, inside the floor cluster, because its work already happened during the build.

top3.label: StyleX without CSS layers (:not() specificity hack)

renderTiming.why: One style recalculation and one layout per lane, so the counts tie and only the recalc cost (0.119-0.465 ms) separates them. A variant toggle changes which class an element carries, not how often Chrome recalculates a static sheet.

payload.why: The css-prop fold ships 3.39 kB gzipped, below `vanilla`'s 3.79 kB, because five variant rules collapse into numbered classes on one element. `bamboo` ships 6.69 kB and `panda`'s recipe 5.79, while `panda`'s `css()` build adds its resolver for 8.76 kB. The utility lanes carry a scanned sheet whatever the page uses, `cnfast` 16.1 kB and `tailwind-merge` 15.1 kB.

nsweep.why: At 4000 buttons the class-toggle concat holds 2.04 ms and `bamboo`'s literal join 2.45, both linear in n. `panda` multiplies its per-element merge by n and reaches 52.3 ms, 21× `bamboo` on the same API. `emotion` (11.3 ms) and `styled-components` (7.03 ms) scale their hash the same way.
